process_area.title: Sales Enablement Strategy, Content & Coaching Framework

value_stream.name: Sales Enablement, Product Knowledge Mastery & Clienteling

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Store Ops (links to VS-07), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Marketing (links to VS-14), L&D (links to VS-19.4), HR (links to VS-19/VS-103), In-Store Services (links to VS-09), Finance (links to VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Annual strategy (links to VS-33.1); capability review

workflows.name: Sales Enablement Strategy, Operating Model & Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "capture, service attach" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve the enablement budget" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: enablement strategy; operational: KPI linkage
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-owner risk**: Selling quality varies by store with no program; mitigated by enablement strategy
- **Misaligned-incentive risk**: Enablement not tied to commercial outcomes; mitigated by KPI linkage
System Touchpoints: - Store ops (links to VS-07); merchandising (links to VS-01); marketing (links to VS-14); L&D (links to VS-19.4); finance (links to VS-17.4); strategy (links to VS-33)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Store-Ops define the sales-enablement strategy: target selling outcomes (basket size, conversion, attach rate, trade-pro capture, service attach), the capability model for associates (product knowledge + selling skills + clienteling + tools), the operating model (central enablement team + store-level coaches), and KPIs aligned to merchandise/commercial plan (links to VS-101/VS-33.2)

Sales Enablement establish governance: enablement steering (Store Ops, Merchandising, Marketing, L&D, HR), cadence, integration to L&D (links to VS-19.4), merchandising (links to VS-01.1 assortment/pricing), and marketing campaigns (links to VS-14.1), and the link to incentive/compensation (links to VS-102/W3838)
COO/Executive ratify the strategy, approve the enablement budget (links to W3840), and cascade to store/category leadership as a commercial priority

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, L&D (links to VS-19.4), Store Ops (links to VS-07), In-Store Services (links to VS-09), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Master Associates, Trade Capability (links to VS-123)

workflows.name: Selling-Skills Curriculum & Consultative Selling Playbook Development

Controls: - CTL-601 (ensure controlled execution — Sales Enablement Strategy, Content & Coaching Framework (PA-124.1).)
- operational: tailored playbooks; operational: coaching (links to W3836)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Generic-curriculum risk**: Selling skills not tailored to BuildRight's project/category reality; mitigated by tailored playbooks
- **Adoption-gap risk**: Playbooks published but not used on the floor; mitigated by coaching (links to W3836)
System Touchpoints: - L&D/LMS (links to VS-19.4); enablement platform (links to W3839); in-store services (links to VS-09); merchandising (links to VS-01); design (links to VS-66)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/L&D design the selling-skills curriculum: greeting/needs-discovery, consultative/needs-based selling, objection handling, closing, multi-tender/loyalty enrollment, cross-sell/upsell, and customer-follow-up — distinct from (and complementary to) the trade-product knowledge (links to W3842) and general L&D (links to VS-19.4)

Sales Enablement build consultative selling playbooks for BuildRight's context: project-based selling (a customer building a bathroom/kitchen/extension needs a solution basket, not a single item), problem-solving selling (the customer describes a problem, the associate specifies the solution), and value/quality selling vs price-only — leveraging estimation (links to VS-09.2) and design (links to VS-66)
Sales Enablement/L&D publish the curriculum and playbooks to the enablement/LMS platform (links to W3839/VS-19.4), and refresh for new categories/services/promotions (links to VS-01.1/VS-14)

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Merchandising/Category (links to VS-01), Store Ops (links to VS-07), In-Store Services (links to VS-09), Installation (links to VS-12), L&D (links to VS-19.4)
fields.Trigger: Category strategy (links to VS-01); new product/service
fields.Volume: Department/category playbooks (lumber, tiles, plumbing, electrical, paint, tools, appliances)

workflows.name: Department & Category Selling Playbooks (Attachment, Linked, Project Selling)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "track attach performance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-601 (ensure controlled execution — Sales Enablement Strategy, Content & Coaching Framework (PA-124.1).)
- operational: attach playbooks; operational: update cycle
Pain Points / Risks: - **Missed-attach risk**: Associates sell the primary item but not the basket; mitigated by attach playbooks
- **Stale-playbook risk**: Playbooks not updated for new SKUs/promotions; mitigated by update cycle
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising (links to VS-01); in-store services (links to VS-09); installation (links to VS-12); delivery (links to VS-06/VS-56); warranty (links to VS-53); store comms (links to VS-63); enablement platform (links to W3839)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Merchandising develop department/category selling playbooks: category selling points, common customer jobs, attachment/accessory items (e.g., paint → brushes/rollers/tray/primer/sandpaper; power tool → battery/blade/accessory; tile → adhesive/grout/spacer; lumber → fasteners/finish), complementary categories, and project baskets

Sales Enablement/In-Store-Services embed service attach into the playbooks: fabrication (cut-to-length, pipe threading — links to VS-09.1), paint tinting (links to W898), estimation (links to VS-09.2), installation (links to VS-12), delivery (links to VS-06/VS-56), and warranty/protection (links to VS-53.3) as attach opportunities
Sales Enablement publish and update playbooks (links to W3839), brief store teams on new attachments/promotions (links to VS-14/VS-63 store comms), and track attach performance (links to W3849)

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Store Ops/Regional (links to VS-07), Store Managers, Department Supervisors, L&D (links to VS-19.4), HR (links to VS-103), Mystery Shopping (links to VS-44/W3850)

workflows.name: Sales Coaching, Field Enablement & Store-Level Reinforcement

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Sales Enablement/Store-Ops establish the coaching operating model" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor selling quality via observation, mystery shopping" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-601 (ensure controlled execution — Sales Enablement Strategy, Content & Coaching Framework (PA-124.1).)
- operational: coach-the-coach and tools; operational: coaching cadence and field support
Pain Points / Risks: - **Coaching-inconsistency risk**: Coaching quality varies by store/manager; mitigated by coach-the-coach and tools
- **Time-pressure risk**: Managers too busy to coach; mitigated by coaching cadence and field support
System Touchpoints: - Store ops (links to VS-07); L&D (links to VS-19.4); insights/mystery shopping (links to VS-44); CX/feedback (links to VS-13); recognition (links to W3838)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Store-Ops establish the coaching operating model: store-manager and department-supervisor as front-line coaches, regional/field enablement support, coaching cadence (pre-shift huddles, weekly coaching, monthly review), and coaching tools (observation checklists, call/coaching logs)

Sales Enablement train store managers/supervisors as coaches (coach-the-coach), equip them with the playbooks (links to W3834/W3835) and observation tools, and reinforce selling behaviors on the floor (greeting, needs-discovery, attach, loyalty enrollment, clienteling links to W3844)

Sales Enablement/Store-Ops monitor selling quality via observation, mystery shopping (links to VS-44/W3850), and customer feedback (links to VS-13/W1550), and feed coaching priorities and recognition (links to W3838)

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Trade/B2B Sales (links to VS-11/VS-107), Trade Pro Program (links to VS-43), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Key Account (links to VS-107), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Project/Design (links to VS-66)
fields.Trigger: B2B strategy (links to VS-11/VS-107); trade-pro program (links to VS-43)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "account and contract pricing" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "Sales Enablement/Key-Account enable key-account/enterprise selling" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track trade-pro capture and account growth" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-601 (ensure controlled execution — Sales Enablement Strategy, Content & Coaching Framework (PA-124.1).)
- operational: consultative enablement; operational: identification and enrollment (links to VS-43/VS-13)
Pain Points / Risks: - **B2C-B2B-conflation risk**: Trade-pros served like walk-ins, missing account value; mitigated by consultative enablement
- **Capture-gap risk**: Trade-pros unidentified at POS; mitigated by identification and enrollment (links to VS-43/VS-13)
System Touchpoints: - Trade/B2B (links to VS-11); key account (links to VS-107); trade pro (links to VS-43); B2G (links to VS-46); project/design (links to VS-66); L&D (links to VS-19.4); pricing (links to W163)

steps.a: Sales Enablement Lead / Head of Trade / Account Management
steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Trade-Sales develop trade-pro/B2B consultative selling enablement: understanding trade-pro job economics, project/quotation selling (links to VS-11.2/VS-66.2), account and contract pricing (links to VS-11.1/W163), volume and project baskets, and trade-pro loyalty/value props (links to VS-43) — distinct from B2C selling

Sales Enablement/Key-Account enable key-account/enterprise selling (links to VS-107): account-team selling, executive engagement, solution/program selling, and bid/tender response (links to VS-46 for B2G)

Sales Enablement/L&D deliver trade-pro/B2B selling certification and coaching for Pro-Desk/trade-focused associates and account teams, and track trade-pro capture and account growth (links to W3849/VS-107)

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, HR/Compensation (links to VS-102), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Marketing (links to VS-14), Payroll (links to VS-19.2), Recognition (links to W630)

workflows.name: Sales Contest, Incentive & Motivation Program Design

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "Sales Enablement/HR/Finance design sales contests and incentives aligned to" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track leaderboards transparently, and sustain motivation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-measure of "measure contest ROI" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-601 (ensure controlled execution — Sales Enablement Strategy, Content & Coaching Framework (PA-124.1).)
- operational: contest rules pre-cleared against discount-abuse controls (W1475); normalized scoring for store-size equity
Pain Points / Risks: - **Gaming risk**: Incentives drive undesirable behavior (e.g., over-selling, discount abuse); mitigated by design and controls (links to VS-23/W1475)
- **Inequity risk**: Contests favor high-volume stores; mitigated by equitable/normalized design
System Touchpoints: - Compensation (links to VS-102); payroll (links to VS-19.2); finance (links to VS-17.4); store comms (links to VS-63); recognition (links to W630); marketing (links to VS-14)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/HR/Finance design sales contests and incentives aligned to commercial priorities (attach, basket size, trade-pro capture, category push, slow-mover clearance links to VS-64), with equitable access across stores/roles, lawful and within budget (links to VS-102/VS-17.4)
Sales Enablement/Marketing launch and communicate contests (store comms links to VS-63, recognition links to W630), track leaderboards transparently, and sustain motivation

Sales Enablement/Payroll administer incentive payout (links to VS-19.2/W1001 profit-sharing where applicable), measure contest ROI (sales lift vs incentive cost — links to W3849), and iterate the incentive design

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, IT (links to VS-27/VS-113), Enterprise Architecture (links to VS-113), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Mobile App (links to VS-75), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Analytics (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Volume: Enablement tech stack (LMS, mobile, clienteling tool)

workflows.name: Sales Enablement Technology & Content Delivery Platform

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "Sales Enablement/IT/EA manage the enablement technology stack" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-update of "Sales Enablement/IT deliver and update content" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "Sales Enablement/Analytics measure content adoption and effectiveness" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-601 (ensure controlled execution — Sales Enablement Strategy, Content & Coaching Framework (PA-124.1).)
- operational: mobile-first, simple UX; operational: offline capability
Pain Points / Risks: - **Access-friction risk**: Associates can't find content on the floor; mitigated by mobile-first, simple UX
- **Offline-gap risk**: Content unavailable when store connectivity drops; mitigated by offline capability
System Touchpoints: - Mobile/employee app (links to VS-75); L&D/LMS (links to VS-19.4); enterprise architecture (links to VS-113); IT ops (links to VS-27); analytics (links to VS-28.1); store comms (links to VS-63)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/IT/EA manage the enablement technology stack: mobile-first content/product-info access for associates on the floor (links to VS-75 employee app), micro-learning and refreshers via LMS (links to VS-19.4), clienteling tool (links to W3844), and quick-reference/playbook access — aligned to enterprise architecture (links to VS-113)

Sales Enablement/IT deliver and update content (playbooks links to W3834/W3835, product knowledge links to W3842, promotions links to VS-14/VS-63) to the floor in near-real-time, and ensure offline-capable access in stores
Sales Enablement/Analytics measure content adoption and effectiveness (views, completion, knowledge-check pass rates, correlation to selling KPIs — links to W3849) and prioritize content

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Finance (links to VS-17.4), Procurement (links to VS-34), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Merchandising (links to VS-01), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Store Ops (links to VS-07), ABC (links to VS-86.3)
fields.Trigger: Annual budget (links to VS-33.1); vendor cycle; review

workflows.name: Sales Enablement Budget, Vendor/Partner Governance & Continuous Improvement

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Sales Enablement/Finance develop the enablement budget" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-allocate of "reallocate budget to highest-impact enablement" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-601 (ensure controlled execution — Sales Enablement Strategy, Content & Coaching Framework (PA-124.1).)
- operational: ROI analytics; operational: ABC and brand-neutrality
Pain Points / Risks: - **ROI-opacity risk**: Enablement spend unmeasured; mitigated by ROI analytics
- **Vendor-influence risk**: Vendor-funded enablement biases selling; mitigated by ABC and brand-neutrality
System Touchpoints: - Finance (links to VS-17.4); procurement (links to VS-34); legal (links to VS-100.3); ABC (links to VS-86.3); analytics (links to VS-28.1); strategy (links to VS-33)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Finance develop the enablement budget: content production, coaching/field team, technology (links to W3839), contests/incentives (links to W3838), and vendor-funded enablement; align to annual budget (links to VS-33.1/VS-17.4)

Sales Enablement/Procurement/Legal govern enablement vendors/partners (training providers, content, mystery-shopping links to VS-44), vendor-funded enablement (compliant with ABC links to VS-86.3 and brand-neutrality), and contracts/SLAs (links to W688/VS-100.3)
Sales Enablement/Analytics run continuous improvement: measure enablement ROI (links to W3849), gather store/associate feedback, and reallocate budget to highest-impact enablement
